deep.reconstruction:
The page studies the one-parameter family of septic polynomials
  F(x) = x^7 - 28x^4 + 280 + 200 cos(phi),
where phi is a parameter (presumably an angle, so cos(phi) lies in [-1, 1]). The aim is to locate the stationary point of F and decide the sign of F there, which tells how many real roots F has as phi varies.

Step 1 (derivative; this step is implicit and filled in by me):
  F'(x) = 7x^6 - 112x^3 = 7x^3(x^3 - 16).
  The stationary points are x = 0 and x = 16^(1/3).
  Gauss writes the second one: x = cbrt(16).

Step 2 (value at the stationary point; the reduction is mine). With x^3 = 16:
  x^7 = x^6 * x = 256 * cbrt(16)
  28x^4 = 28 * 16 * cbrt(16) = 448 * cbrt(16)
  so x^7 - 28x^4 = -192 * cbrt(16).
  Gauss writes '-192 cbrt16 + 200 cos phi' with 280 placed alongside. He then combines these into F(cbrt16) = 280 - 192 cbrt(16) + 200 cos(phi).
  Since F'' = 42x^5 - 336x^2 = 42x^2(x^3 - 8) > 0 at x^3 = 16, this point is the minimum of F on x > 0 (justification mine).

Step 3 (evaluating 192 cbrt16 with logarithms):
  log10(192) = 2.28330
  log10(cbrt16) = (1/3) log10(16) = 0.40137. This is the struck-out figure, apparently first miswritten.
  The sum is 2.68467, giving 192 cbrt16 = 483.81.

Step 4 (normalising by 200):
  280/200 = 1.4
  483.81/200 = 2.419
  1.4 - 2.419 = -1.019
  Hence F(cbrt16)/200 = cos(phi) - 1.019.

Conclusion (implicit; my interpretation): since cos(phi) <= 1 < 1.019, the minimum value is negative for every phi, at worst about -3.8 when phi = 0. F is positive at x = 0, since 280 + 200cos phi >= 80, and tends to +infinity as x grows. So F always has exactly two positive real roots, one on each side of cbrt(16) = 2.52.

This fits the previous page, which lists numerical roots of a septic: complex pairs together with a real root '+2'. That is consistent with F(2) = -40 + 200 cos phi = 0 when cos phi = 0.2, though the link is my conjecture. The page is a quick check on the real-root structure of the parametrised equation being solved numerically there.
errors: No substantive errors. The struck-out figure under 2.28330 seems to be a miswritten log10(cbrt16) = 0.40137, corrected in the sum 2.68467.
Gauss does not write out the derivative, the second-derivative check, or the conclusion. These are inferred.

results.what: Stationary point of x^7 - 28x^4 at x = cbrt(16), with value -192*cbrt(16). This gives the minimum of F as 280 - 192 cbrt16 + 200 cos(phi) = 200(cos(phi) - 1.019) < 0 for all phi, so there are always two positive real roots.
results.modern_name: Elementary calculus / real-root counting via the extremum (discriminant-type sign check)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine scratch calculation: an extremum of a parametrised septic is evaluated with log tables to check the sign of the minimum. It contains no new method or result.

checkable.asserts: The real stationary points are 0 and 16**(1/3).
The value at cbrt(16) is -192*cbrt(16), so this simplifies to 0.
The minimum is still negative at cos(phi) = 1 (about -3.81), so there are two positive real roots for all phi.

transcription_corrections: The struck-out number under 2.28330 is probably 40137, i.e. log10 cbrt16 = 0.40137, rather than '40477'.
'68467' should be read as 2.68467 = log10(192 cbrt16), the sum of the two logarithms.
The figures 1,4 / -2.419 / -1,019 are 280/200, 192cbrt16/200, and their difference.
